key_insight: Variational quantum circuits can look statistically random long before they become untrainable, so complexity and trainability are not the same thing.
engineering_relevance: For NISQ algorithm design, this means random-like diagnostics alone should not be treated as a warning sign of barren plateaus or failed optimization.
method: Evaluate structured variational circuits on the 1D cluster-Ising model and a generalized toric code Hamiltonian.
Track complexity with Porter-Thomas statistics, entanglement-spectrum level statistics, and inverse participation ratios.
Compare these diagnostics against variational optimization behavior as circuit depth increases.
evidence_signal: As depth increases, the circuits move toward random-state or random-matrix-like signatures while optimization remains effective and gradients do not show exponential suppression in the studied regime.
watch_item: The results are limited to finite-depth structured circuits and the specific models studied, so stronger randomization or different ansätze may still trigger barren plateaus.
paper_title: Separation of Statistical Complexity and Trainability in Variational Quantum Circuits
